newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ dollar ends on buoyant note after RB statement.
newsitem.headline: NZ dollar ends on buoyant note after RB statement.

text.p: Buoyed by a hawkish Reserve Bank statement, the New Zealand dollar ended strongly on Friday and was poised to test fresh eight year highs, dealers said.

"In the next couple of weeks, the ongoing demand we are seeing from Asian and European counterparties all point to a test very close to 70 (US) cents before we can see any sort of down move," a chief dealer said.
The bank took the market by surprise in its six monthly economic projections with its slightly higher inflation profile as well as its comments on the Trade-Weighted Index projections.
Many dealers had been expecting an implicit easing but little was forthcoming.
The Kiwi ended at 5.00 p.m. at US$0.6955/62 from its 0.6934 low before the statement.
The TWI, which the bank forecast to be at a constant 65.0 through the three-year forecast period, ended at 66.07 compared with 65.84 at the opening.

The bank also assumed that 90-day bank bills would hold up at 10.0 percent through the forecast period and dealers said that that would underpin the currency despite any desire by the bank to change the mix of monetary conditions in favour of a
lower currency and firmer interest rates.

"Clearly the Reserve Bank would like to see a lower currency on a TWI basis and when that easing does come they would like to see that facilitated through a weaker currency rather than through lower interest rates," the chief dealer said.

"But the problem they have is: are they going to get it? With interest rate differentials clearly in favour of the Kiwi and real interest rates very high here, it becomes a major problem for them," he said.

Eventually the bank may get what it wants as the economy slows but "that's some time away", he added. "In the meantime, it doesn't look as though they will get the mix they want in the foreseeable future."
The coming October 12 election may also disturb predictions.
